newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Friday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Friday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Friday:

Spokesman Jean-Christophe Filori said Monday's Research Council would focus on the fifth RTD framework programme, research on BSE and financial supplement to the fourth framework programme. Filori said discussions would also cover the follow-up to the green paper on innovation and the action plan on learning in the information society.

Spokeswoman Sophie Petzell said an exchange of information on drugs was taking place in Brussels which had been opened by Commissioner Gradin. Petzell underlined the fact that every speaker so far had raised the issue of synthetic drugs and had asked to make it one of the priority in the fight against drugs.
Spokeswoman Barbara Nolan announced a week on safety and health starting on Monday.

Spokesman Jochen Kubosch said that the Commission had authorised, on the advice of the agency for the evaluation of pharmaceutical products based in London, the circulation of two drugs to treat AIDS -- the Crixivan and the Invirase.

In answer to a question, spokesman Willy Helin confirmed that the Commission was still discussing a paper at service level on the revision of the regulation on airline slots allocation but said no decision had been made yet.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/96/887: 52 million Ecus for cross-border cooperation between Corsica, Sardigna and Toscane.
- IP/96/889: Producers must respect animal welfare - Franz Fischler.
- IP/96/890: Japanese liquor tax, statement by the European Commission.
- IP/96/891: First European week on safety and health, 7-13 October - making Europe a better place to work.
- Speech/96/235: Speech by Commission President Jacques Santer on the European Union and Japan, common interest and shared challenges.
- Eurostat: Net earnings of employees in manufacturing industry in the EU - 1996.
- Memo/96/93: Calendar of the week of October 7 to October 13, 1996.
